newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK govt paper dips with overnight fall in U.S..
newsitem.headline: HK govt paper dips with overnight fall in U.S..

text.p: Hong Kong government paper dipped on Friday in line with the overnight fall in treasuries in the United States, dealers said.
"The yields went up in line with movement in the U.S.," a dealer with a foreign bank said.
Yields of the one-week Exchange Fund bill rose to 4.47 percent from 4.44.
But yields on the three-year note eased to 6.21 percent from 6.22 on Thursday, while seven-year notes yielded 6.94 percent versus 6.96.
The longest 10-year notes yielded 7.375 percent versus 7.18.
Interbank market rates dipped slightly as liquidity rose, although dealers said the market stayed relatively quiet.
Overnight cash eased slightly to 4-5/8 9/16 percent from 4-9/16 7/16 and three-month money stood at 5-1/2 7/16 percent from 5-7/16 5/16.
